profile.reading:
This registry entry, listed under the name Delivery Emergency Response Center and attributed to the utility PSE&G, sits on Park Avenue in Bridgewater Township, Somerset County, New Jersey. PSE&G, formally Public Service Electric and Gas Company, is part of the PSEG family of companies and is New Jersey's largest electric and gas utility. Within PSE&G, Delivery is the business unit responsible for the physical distribution of electricity and natural gas to customers, as distinct from PSEG's separate power generation business.

An emergency response center, in utility terminology, is typically a coordination facility used to stage crews, dispatch trucks, and manage restoration efforts during storms, gas leaks, and other outage events, rather than a facility built to house servers or IT equipment for third party customers. PSE&G's own public materials describe extensive storm response and outage tracking infrastructure across its New Jersey service territory, consistent with that function, but do not name or describe a specific Bridgewater facility by this title.

No square footage, power capacity, tenancy, or construction history for this specific building is published by PSE&G, and none was found in available public records. Based on its name and its operator's line of business, this location reads as utility grid operations infrastructure rather than as a conventional data center, and it is presented here on that basis.

reading: PSE&G, the regulated New Jersey electric and gas utility subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Group and headquartered in Newark, is primarily an energy infrastructure provider to data centers rather than a data center operator in its own right. The company's published Data Center Solutions offering provides tailored high-voltage electrical service, at 138kV, 230kV, and 345kV depending on facility needs, to data center customers in New Jersey and PSEG's Long Island and Rockaways, New York service territory, requiring dedicated land parcels of 2.5 to 7 acres depending on voltage level to support hyperscale and cloud computing facilities that now demand 200 to 300 watts per square foot compared to 20 to 30 watts for legacy computing loads. Because PSE&G's core business is utility infrastructure rather than data center operations or colocation, this registry's New Jersey facility record under the PSE&G name most likely reflects the company's own grid or network operations infrastructure rather than a commercial data center serving outside tenants, a distinction important for accurately classifying PSE&G relative to the wholesale and colocation operators that make up most of this registry's other New Jersey facilities, such as fifteenfortyseven Critical Systems Realty and GlobeNet.
